To run a pellet smoker overnight (8–12 hours), I recommend a portable power station with at least 500Wh capacity, ideally 700–1,000Wh for extra safety margin.

Pellet smokers are relatively power-efficient once running. Most electricity goes toward the auger, fan, controller, and ignition rod—not directly heating the cooking chamber.

How much power do you need?

Typical pellet smoker estimates:

Operation

	

Power consumption




Startup / ignition

	

200–400W




Normal smoking

	

30–80W average




8-hour smoke

	

240–640Wh




12-hour smoke

	

360–960Wh

These are planning estimates; actual consumption depends on the smoker, weather, and temperature setting.

My recommendation: Choose a LiFePO4 power station with a pure sine wave AC inverter rated for at least 500W. A 1,000Wh model is a particularly good choice for a 12-hour overnight smoke.

For example, at a 50W smoker draw plus 10W inverter overhead, a 1,000Wh station with 85% usable energy would run for approximately 14 hours. Real-world results will vary. Traeger's published specifications confirm that electrical demand differs substantially by grill model. 
Traeger Support

For an unattended overnight cook, test the full setup beforehand, use independent temperature alarms, and keep the battery sheltered from rain and away from smoker heat.

One question

What brand and model is your pellet smoker? (Traeger, Pit Boss, Recteq, Camp Chef, Z Grills, etc.)

I can estimate the battery size needed for a full 12-hour smoke much more accurately with that information.
